searchLog: Read profile.md, target-companies.json, sent-log.json (last ~40 'opportunities' entries, Sept 4-13: Sierra APX/SWE-Agent/early-career and Anthropic Fellows/Applied-AI-Evangelist all recently sent, so this run planned to rotate to Databricks, Stripe, Meta, Scale AI, Ramp, Cohere, OpenAI, Notion), applications.json (empty), and life/PIPELINE.md for exclusions (IBM x6, Claude Corps, Ford FCG, Red Ventures, TikTok, Goldman Sachs, CIL, MIT Future Fest, MLH, Horizon, 3x Adobe, Micron, Kalshi, MATS, Anthropic Fellows July cohort, Northslope, Last Mile, Yale SOM, Tuck Business Bridge). Checked life/PROFILE.md for the graduation-date conflict flagged in this run's instructions: both morning-briefing/profile.md and life/PROFILE.md now independently state December 2026, resolved 2026-08-04 -- no live conflict; the instructions describing an 'unsettled Aug-Dec 2026' split are themselves stale and should be updated at the source. Before spending search/fetch budget, sanity-checked both tools: WebSearch works (surfaced a real, plausible lead -- Databricks 'Associate Product Manager, New Grad (2027 Start)', SF/Mountain View/Bellevue, grad Fall 2026 or Spring 2027, $133-150k -- matching target-companies.json's note that this req was already live). WebFetch is completely non-functional: 8 distinct hosts tried (databricks.com, stripe.com, metacareers.com, job-boards.greenhouse.io, api.ashbyhq.com x3, notion.com, and even www.anthropic.com itself) all returned EGRESS_BLOCKED before any request reached the destination. Per the proxy's own diagnostic doc this is an organization-level egress policy denial, not a transient or per-host issue, and the instructions say to report it rather than route around it (no curl/raw-TCP workaround was attempted). hunt.md requires confirming from the actual application page that applications are open and Dom is eligible -- a search snippet is explicitly disallowed as sole evidence -- so even the promising Databricks lead could not be verified and is correctly omitted. Zero verified opportunities is the honest output. This is the same failure this repo's own hunt commit history shows on essentially every run back to 2026-08-18/19 (see git log 'hunt:' commits) -- close to a month of consecutive days where WebFetch has been blocked and no opportunity could be verified, unfixed across every prior report. This is an environment/org-level network-policy problem, not a lack of findable roles or a search-budget issue, and needs a human to allowlist outbound job-board/careers domains (or grant broader egress) in this environment's network policy configuration.
